summary: Pre-Vote update required a model change; the updated model and rebased harness validate 17 fresh traces, and model checking found two reproduced defects: a Pre-Vote round survives leader establishment and makes the new leader re-elect, and a stale Pre-Vote grant from a removed voter panics RaftCore.
validation_limits: LIMITED_COVERAGE: bounded three-node model (MaxTerm 2, MaxLogIndex 4, at most 2 election starts, 2 Pre-Vote starts, 2 membership appends, 1 crash, 1 drop, 5 in-flight messages; hunt configs narrow unrelated faults); every BFS run stopped at its 30-minute budget with a non-empty queue and every simulation is time-bounded, so no run is an exhaustive pass.
No fairness or liveness property is claimed.

Trace validation covers 17 engine-level traces (20 events) driven by test fixtures; runtime-only behavior (tick timing, the in-flight-round rate limiter, the RPC timeout, transport errors, the default-grant network implementation) is abstracted; HandlePreVoteResponseTally/Stale/NonMember are model-checked but not observed in traces.
Open and discharge checks depend on the EnvUpdate rely (v3) and are bounded; the open model is not exhaustive.

Followers' membership replication is not modeled (inherited abstraction), so the follower variant of MC-2 is covered by the integration reproduction only; the transfer bit of leadership-transfer elections is not propagated in the inherited model (independent of this update).

Two inherited model defects were repaired in this run (absent-log LogLE equality; HandleVoteResponse lease effects); the prior suite's three-voter MC results were vacuous for leader paths and are not reused.
Upstream novelty of MC-1/MC-2 is undetermined: issue trackers and history were not searched under the isolation contract.

findings.title: Pre-Vote round started while Candidate survives leader establishment and makes the new leader re-elect
findings.cause: establish_leader/become_leader do not reset Engine.pre_candidate, and handle_pre_vote_resp calls elect() on a Pre-Vote quorum without checking that the node is still the non-leader whose vote the round probed; a Candidate can start such a round because the tick skips only Leaders and Trigger::elect(true) has no role check.
findings.trigger: A Candidate at term T starts a Pre-Vote round (election timer or Trigger::elect(true)) while its real vote replies are in flight; a peer grants both the real vote and the term T+1 Pre-Vote (its uncommitted vote carries no lease); the real grant arrives first and the node becomes Leader at T; the Pre-Vote grant is delivered afterwards, within the RPC timeout.
findings.consequence: The freshly established Leader abandons term T and starts an election at T+1 that peers holding its lease reject, leaving the cluster without a working leader for at least a lease and inflating the term (the disruption Pre-Vote is documented to prevent); with debug assertions the stale Leader object trips Engine::try_leader_handler and RaftCore panics.

premises: A node can start a Pre-Vote round while it is a Candidate: handle_tick_election skips only ServerState::Leader and ExternalCommand::Elect{pre_vote:true} checks only voter membership.
Leader establishment (establish_leader -> update_vote -> become_leader) does not reset Engine.pre_candidate; only do_elect and become_following do.
A peer that granted the real vote holds an uncommitted vote without leader lease and therefore grants the term+1 Pre-Vote.
Message delay may deliver the Pre-Vote grant after the real-vote grant within the vote RPC timeout (election_timeout_min).
Pre-Vote is enabled (Config::enable_pre_vote / runtime toggle) or requested per call with Trigger::elect(true).

findings.title: Stale Pre-Vote grant from a node outside the current round's voter set panics RaftCore
findings.cause: Pre-Vote responses are correlated only by the pre-candidate leader id, which every round started from the same local vote shares, while each round freezes its own voter set; handle_pre_vote_resp passes any matching grant to Candidate::grant_by, which expects the granter to be in that set.
findings.trigger: A node runs a Pre-Vote round while peer P is a voter and P's grant is delayed; the voter set changes so that P is no longer a voter; the node starts another round from the same local vote (e.g. Trigger::elect(true), or the tick); P's delayed grant arrives within the RPC timeout.
findings.consequence: grant_by's expect("target not in quorum set") panics and the node's RaftCore task terminates (follower or leader; debug and release builds), so the node stops serving until restarted.

premises: Two Pre-Vote rounds started from the same local vote have the same correlation key (does_pre_candidate_vote_match compares leader ids only).
Each round's progress tracker contains only the voters frozen at pre_elect, and grant_by expects the granter to be one of them.
The voter set can change between two such rounds without changing the local vote (leader-proposed membership change; a follower learns it by AppendEntries with an equal vote).
A delayed grant can be delivered within the vote RPC timeout (election_timeout_min) after the second round started.

findings.title: pre_vote.md backward-compatibility paragraph contradicts the implemented transport-error semantics
findings.cause: docs/protocol/pre_vote.md says the default pre_vote returns Unreachable and that Unreachable counts as a grant; the code's default returns a synthesized grant and never counts a transport error as a grant.
findings.trigger: Reading the documentation; at runtime an Unreachable Pre-Vote reply is not a grant (shipped test pre_vote_unreachable_peer_is_not_a_grant).
findings.consequence: None in the implementation: the code behavior is the intended one (comments, network trait docs, Config docs, tests); only the prose is stale and should be corrected.
